Improves rendering quality for articulated humans.
Computationally more expensive than standard NeRF due to multi-view processing and attention.
*   **When to use:** Dynamic human rendering where multi-view consistency and geometric priors are beneficial.
*   **When not to use:** Static scenes without articulated subjects, or resource-constrained environments where SMPL inference and multi-view attention are too costly.
The method originates from the "Neural Human Performer" paper, which introduces a framework for learning generalizable radiance fields for human performance rendering.
